doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Starting the Rosie O'Grady's band and the 1990 Classic Jazz Band
summary: Allred explains his band began in 1990 from the Rosie O'Grady's music hall house band he opened in 1974, playing Dixieland and swing with show business touches.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Done a little bit of everything.
Yeah. Well I want to congratulate you on — last I read your band has been together for 25 plus years.

Yeah. We started in 1990, kind of a strange way we fabricated that group you know. Most of us were performing at a music hall called Rosie O’Grady’s, which was in downtown Orlando in the Church Street Station area. And it was a music hall but yet the guy that ran it, who is still around, Bob Snow, had a band there. We had two principal singers, we had dancers, and we had a 7-, sometimes 8-piece band every night of the week you know.

And it lasted for 20 some years. I wasn’t there — I opened it in ’74, put the band together with some guys that I knew in town and some guys that both worked at Disney as well. And some of us stayed on for a while, stayed working at Disney days and continued working nights at this Rosie O’Grady’s club, just to see if it would catch on. And of course it was an unbelievable success from day one, you know, I mean packed. Lines around the block you know.

We were playing Dixieland and some swing. Maybe an occasional pop tune. Not much though. And my thing was it’s got to be good, you know. If it’s just a funny hat band, I don’t know, I’d rather have a good band and do the show biz stuff. That was my philosophy.
You’d rather have a good band than do the show biz stuff?

Both, but we found that we could salute this and salute that and do the songs and do the Sophie Tucker stuff, whatever, Dixieland, and still put out a quality product. And we got a lot of applause for that.
